The main cons for us with AppAttest is that this framework supported only on iOS 14+, but we have  deployment target iOS 13+. So we need implement two solutions to support all iOS versions. And for iOS under 14 it might be [https://developer.apple.com/documentation/devicecheck|https://developer.apple.com/documentation/devicecheck|smart-link]  (DeviceCkeck).
*Question*: Will we support two implementations or we just skip compatibility ckeck for < iOS 14?


*Pros*:

* protects against of reply attack:  “The additional {{clientDataHash}} parameter of the attestation request is not related to the attestation process itself, but extremely important for it to make it safe. As it is, this request is susceptible to a *replay attack* where a hacker could intercept the validation request and steal the attestation object sent from Apple so that later they can "replay" the same validation request at a fake version of your app to make the server believe it came from the real one.
A solution to this problem is to simply not allow the validation request to be executed freely. Instead, the client can provide a one-time use token (or session ID) that the server will expect to accompany the request to ensure its validity. If the same token is used twice, the request will fail. That's what {{clientDataHash}} is for: By providing a hashed version of that expected token to the attestation request, Apple will embed it into the final object and provide your server a way to extract it. With this, it's pretty hard for a hacker to create a compromised version of your app by simply intercepting requests.“
* Could increase anti-tampering protection as additional layer of
security (but it’s a first layer of security for us). There was a suggestion to use RASP also. For example there is free libs [https://github.com/securing/IOSSecuritySuite|https://github.com/securing/IOSSecuritySuite|smart-link]  [https://github.com/talsec/Free-RASP-iOS|https://github.com/talsec/Free-RASP-iOS|smart-link]  And there is more professional sdk which cost might be requested [https://www.guardsquare.com/runtime-application-self-protection-rasp|https://www.guardsquare.com/runtime-application-self-protection-rasp|smart-link] 
*Question*: will we implement RASP to detect if device is jailbroken? If we do, we need extra investigation which RASP sdk is good for us.


*Cons*:

* Not possible to validate if Application is already running on compromised device
* If device has been JailBroken after the key attestation, all new assertions are
tampered - not possible detect it even using Apple’s fraud metric
* Useless against application's behaviour modification with Runtime Instrumentation Frameworks/Debugger
* supports only ios14+


Also the *question* to BE maybe, do we cover all requests with AppAttest (sending attestation)? Or we cover just some part of requests? Which ones?
Also there is a details, which might be note by BE, Apple suggesting to use different generated keys for different users, so could we also check on BE that there is no different users which has the same public keys?

Estimation might be changed depends on answers to questions, but if we support only iOS 14, don’t add RASP checks estimation might be around 1 week or so.

I thought of another possible (and easier to implement) solution to reduce the risk of starvation:

* for an {{order O}} ready for pickup, after computing the costs of all (courier, {{order O}}) pairs, *we subtract the minimum cost from all costs*. This will ensure that there will be a ({{courier C, order O}}) pair with cost 0, decreasing the chances for another order to have a lower cost for that same courier C. Decreasing all the costs for that order (by subtracting the min cost) we also increase the chances of it to be paired with another courier if by chance there was another order that also had cost 0 with the same courier C.
* more generally, if we don’t want to wait for an order to become ready for pickup, we can have a percentage (of the min cost) to be subtracted from all the costs of an order, computed linearly based on the remaining time for cooking (when remaining time is max we subtract 0% of the min cost, when remaining time is 0 we subtract 100% of the min cost)

The query to be used for data backfilling once UI Changes are also integrated for the new flow is as follows:


{noformat}UPDATE taxify_subscription_marketplace.offer oldOfferWithoutCountryCity, (
	SELECT o.id, 
    (CASE WHEN oc.data->>'$.country'!= 'null' THEN oc.data->>'$.country' ELSE  NULL END) as oc_country, 
    (CASE WHEN oc.data->>'$.city_id'!= 'null' THEN oc.data->>'$.city_id' ELSE NULL END) as oc_city
	FROM taxify_subscription_marketplace.offer o
	INNER JOIN taxify_subscription_marketplace.offer_condition oc ON oc.offer_id = o.id and oc.data->>'$.country'!= 'null'
) AS OfferWithExistingConditions
SET oldOfferWithoutCountryCity.country = OfferWithExistingConditions.oc_country, 
	oldOfferWithoutCountryCity.city_id = OfferWithExistingConditions.oc_city
WHERE 
    oldOfferWithoutCountryCity.id = OfferWithExistingConditions.id;{noformat}

Idea for later: add integration with Directory Service. If alert wasn’t matched with any channel defined in alerting system, currently we just produce a warning saying {{Alert has not matched any channel!}}, which is then sent to Alerting’s alerting channel ({{#alerting-alerting}} 🙂). Instead, before doing that we could go to Directory Service and ask for code owner’s support channel, so that we could notify the code owner at least somehow that their alerting channel has not been properly set up yet. In case we cannot send it to the support channel (support channel does not exist), we could then publish the same message to some global chat, like {{#dev-backend}}, asking the team to create/update both support channel in Directory Service and alerting channel 🙂

Next step in DS integration would be to integrate channel list when configuring Slack channels in alerting. In DS we already have a possibility to add multiple Slack channels for a single team (although UX could be improved a bit). We could then introduce a limitation that all channel mappings configured in alerting should use exclusively Slack channels for the specific code owner defined in DS. This way more of team’s channels will be listed in DS.

Would’ve created stories if this epic was in PAW, but it’s not yet, so those are ideas for stories.

Currently, the models (whether OpenAI or internal, trained on OpenAI outputs) act mostly as a productivity enhancing tool for customer support agents, who comprise the bulk (90%+) of CS decisions - so there is generally a lot of human review and fallbacks for classifications available. 

With that being said, in the <10% of cases where models can affect full automations, any _prediction drift_ from OpenAI side could affect CS decisions. But I don’t see a critical vulnerability here, it might affect customer satisfaction scores, but no risk to security in the strict sense of the word. And likely human fallbacks would kick in here as well. It’s similar to a scenario where any other major prediction API (e.g. Google Maps) starts performing badly - a short term hit to product performance that can be mitigated with fallbacks.

Allowances for mothers are granted by the *employer*, according to the legislation in force.

The *State* can also grant social vouchers for mothers, material support for newborns, especially for mothers with low or no income, those in risk situations, those who are victims of domestic violence etc

*Emergency ordinance no. 49/2019, which regulates RH services in Romania*, provides the following:

Art. 2: e) driver = *owner or employee of an alternative transport operator*

Therefore, the driver is either self-employed or must have a contractual relationship with the transport operator and benefit from all the rights provided by Romanian labour legislation.

The relationship between Bolt and drivers is not a direct one. Bolt works with fleets that have employment/collaboration contracts with drivers. Fleets sign T&Cs with Bolt by which they assume responsibility for their drivers. 

Given the contractual relationship between the fleets and the drivers, regulated by the law, I think there shouldn’t be any risks of reclassification, right, [~accountid:62d7b457807cf6f78ca9d117] ? I think that these gifts will have to be offered through fleets and not directly to the driver by Bolt. In any case, the fact that RH is legislated in Romania, there should be no risk of reclassification.

I also think that, in order to make sure that there are no accusations that we financially support the employees of the fleets, instead of money, it would be safer to directly offer the gift ([~accountid:5f2cfe232aa2500028d741b9] ) a basket with products for children, as a good will gesture. |Provider|GMV is from raw table source {{ng_delivery.delivery_order_order}}, with timestamp in UTC+0.

Hey [~accountid:5c010fa68ce9b546efc49454] !

Our policy for video surveillance can be found on Confluence[ here|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/LEG/pages/3489661435/Policy+on+using+video+surveillance+on+the+premises+of+Bolt].

The steps to take are the following:

# *Legal basis and purpose of the video surveillance:*
The legal basis for processing data through CCTV is legitimate interest (GDPR art 6 (1) f)). Legitimate interest requires at first step that the purposes of using cameras are identified which you have stated is safety reasons. 
# *Checking employees' performance and using footage for performance reviews*
This falls under monitoring employees and +this should not be conducted as there are other less privacy intrusive means available+ for the employer to check employee performance. Continuous video monitoring of employees is only likely to be justified in rare circumstances as this is considered highly intrusive in practice. 
# *Positioning the cameras*
The location and positioning of the video cameras has to take into account the legitimate expectations of the data subject to their privacy. Therefore monitoring is +not to be expected in recreational areas, sanitary areas, changing rooms+ etc.
The positioning of the video cameras should be aimed to record areas which correspond to possible threat (theft, property damage).
# *Audio on cameras*
Audio recording should not be used and must be turned off.
# *Retention time of the recordings*
The retention time should be limited to what is strictly necessary. I.e. time needed to detect possible thefts/damages/unauthorised access/review safety incidents. 
The retention period by default should be 72 hours, unless the Polish law allows for longer retention period and that is indeed needed. [~accountid:62d7b457807cf6f78ca9d117] I think the Polish labour law sets the period to max three months? 
After the retention period set the footage must be deleted automatically.
# *Access control and logs*
Access rules must be put in place on who has access to the footage and every access to footage is logged.
# *Transparency and information requirement*
Information/warning signs should be installed with the following information:
-Information that there is video surveillance in the area (e.g camera picture, “We have video surveillance”)
-Controller (“Controller information”)
-Legal basis: Legitimate interest
-Information of where further information can be found (QR code or link to the [global privacy notice on video surveillance|https://bolt.eu/en/legal/terms-for-video-surveillance]). 
We also have a template signs/stickers which I can share that could be made to stickers once installing the cameras. However I need to understand which entity would be the controller here? [~accountid:62d7b457807cf6f78ca9d117] can you help here determining this? I do believe it is the local subsidiary which decides about the purposes and means of using CCTV. 
# *Data protection agreement with service provider*
If we use third party service providers (for hosting the data etc) then a DPA must be signed with them. Do we plan to have a service provider for cameras (e.g. for hosting) and what is their role or where do we store the data?
# *Notifying employees in workplace rules*
Under Polish Labour Code usage of any surveillance should be covered by workplace regulations. Informing the employees on the actual introduction of the video surveillance is required within two weeks before launch of CCTV. This article provides good overview of those requirements: [https://iapp.org/news/a/poland-regulates-workplace-monitoring/|https://iapp.org/news/a/poland-regulates-workplace-monitoring/|smart-link]. 
# *Documenting the set-up*
When you have decided on the CCTV setup in more detail, then we also need to document this. For that, please fill in the questionnaire found [here|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1NAzCrWNj6NG-SDNibRIv6xYb8i4XPUESNLaatrBKeVY/edit]. Bring out all the premises (addresses) where cameras will be installed etc. 

Thank you!
